Self-supervised contrastive pretraining on a large pool of unlabeled SEM images that includes additive-containing samples, followed by the same oversampled fine-tuning used here, will increase macro-F1 on domain-shifted aging classes (formation and 100 cycles) by at least 3 percentage points relative to the reported EfficientNet-B0 Pre+FT(OS) baseline under an identical labeled target data budget.

Incorporating a gradient-reversal domain-adversarial objective during fine-tuning to enforce additive-invariant representations will increase zero-shot F1 on SEM images with previously unseen electrolyte additive chemistries by at least 0.10 relative to the Pre+FT(OS) baseline while not reducing in-domain F1 by more than 0.02.

Self-supervised contrastive pretraining on a pooled unlabeled SEM corpus spanning compositions, cycle states, and additive conditions, followed by a linear probe trained with ≤10 labeled target images per class, will achieve ≥0.90 macro-F1 on additive-containing classes and exceed ImageNet-initialized two-stage supervised transfer by at least 0.05 macro-F1 under the same label budget.
